description: Local, toll, and interconnected VoIP calling for about 1.9 million lines, including 911 delivery to NG911 system service providers and PSAPs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 911 outages must be reported to affected PSAPs within 30 minutes and to the FCC within 120 minutes (47 CFR 4.9(h), (f)); the clocks keep running during a cyber incident. RPO is the age of the last nightly network element configuration backup
manual_workaround: SBC and softswitch geo-redundancy; reroute 911 trunks to the alternate NG911 ingress; break-glass console access at each regional NOC
dependent_third_parties: NG911 system service providers; SS7 and Diameter signaling hubs; equipment vendors' support
dependent_people_or_facilities: 24x7 NOC; voice core engineers; 6 regional NOC data centers (generators with 72 hours of fuel)
shared_services_and_cross_division_depen: Runs without SYS-G1 (network elements use AAA with local break-glass); needs SYS-C5 for any configuration change

business_process: Network monitoring, outage response, and regulatory outage reporting
description: 24x7 fault monitoring, ticketing, and dispatch; NORS, DIRS, and 911 special facility notices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outage detection drives every Part 4 clock (30-minute PSAP notice; 120-minute NORS notification for wireline; 240 minutes for VoIP 911 outages). Ticket data newer than 1 hour cannot be rebuilt from the network
manual_workaround: Element manager consoles in each regional NOC; telephone bridge with PSAP contact list from the printed binder
shared_services_and_cross_division_depen: Shared platform: the same service assurance instance hosts the Engineering Managed Network Operations tenant (BP-E01) and the Tower Alarm Monitoring Center tenant (BP-T01); one outage stops all three

business_process: Tower lighting monitoring and FAA notification
description: Remote monitoring of obstruction lights on about 6,200 registered antenna structures; FAA outage reports; outage records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A light outage not corrected within 30 minutes must be reported to the FAA immediately (47 CFR 17.48(a)); without the automatic alarm system the owner must observe each structure at least once each 24 hours (17.47(a)(1)). Aviation safety drives the 4-hour MTD
manual_workaround: Fallback to RMU vendor's direct alerting for about 5,100 newer units; field crews for daily visual observation of the rest (procedure not yet written; gap 6)
dependent_third_parties: RMU vendor; cellular carriers for RMU backhaul; FAA (NOTAM system)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Alarm Monitoring Center (24x7); tower field technicians
shared_services_and_cross_division_depen: Depends on the Carrier's service assurance platform (BP-C04). A Carrier containment action that isolates the platform stops lighting alarms

description: Sign-in, MFA, PAM, and identity governance for all 45,000 workforce users and about 2,100 outsourced agents
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every IT application federates to SYS-G1; agents, engineers, and NOC staff cannot reach the OSS, BSS, or SYS-E1 without it
manual_workaround: Sealed break-glass accounts per critical system; network elements fall back to local AAA break-glass
shared_services_and_cross_division_depen: Used by every process except network element call processing
